item.title: Basilisk: A Three-Stage Checker and the One Byte That Undid It
item.description: Three stages, a SHA-256 key schedule, a fake core dump and a GDB stub that lies about the math. The maze is real. The scorer at the end leaves the front door open.

item.title: BlackGateWatch: A DNS Tunnel Hiding in Plain Sight
item.description: Three thousand frames of ordinary corporate DNS, and one workstation quietly hex-encoding data into subdomains of its own domain. No TXT records, no long labels, no obvious tell.

item.title: Gravimetry: Hunting a Flag in Gravitational-Wave Noise
item.description: 41,216 float32 samples of simulated detector strain, a calibration pulse, and a handout decoder that is deliberately broken in two places. The mathed-up path, and the shortcut that saved the afternoon.

item.title: JANUS: The Cipher Had Two Faces, but the Checker Only Needed One
item.description: A mutated stream cipher on the outside, a four-byte repeating key on the inside. Disassemble the scorer and the whole thing falls apart in a dozen instructions.

item.title: Sidedoor: The Cloud Backup That Was Uploading the Secret
item.description: A pcap full of normal traffic and one host quietly posting a backup file to a cloud sync endpoint over plain HTTP. The recovery token is in the upload. No crypto required.

item.title: The Signal Key: Hermes Hides in the Bundle
item.description: A React Native app gates a licence screen behind a string table, a rotator and a small block cipher. Everything needed to reproduce it ships inside index.android.bundle.

item.title: THORNWALL: Anti-Debug Theatre and a Scorer That Talks
item.description: A protector that checks for TracerPid, hashes its own code, and threatens a trap path if you patch a single byte. Then the official scorer hands you the flag under a one-byte XOR.

item.title: Wraith: Unwrapping the Bytecode VM Inside a 2 KB wasm Module
item.description: A 2 KB WebAssembly file with one exported function and two imports. No strings, no symbols, nothing readable. Inside it hides a tiny bytecode VM that checks the flag one byte at a time, and every check inverts in closed form.

item.title: Pearl Harbour: A Forged Captain and a Capability That Sailed to Root
item.description: A tiny Flask app called the Pacific Fleet Cargo and Manifest Registry. It hands out guest JWTs, trusts the kid and alg fields in the header, and shells out to pdftotext with a filename I control. Three mistakes later: root.

item.title: Nexus: When Every Field Lies, Trust the Scorer
item.description: A custom hash chain, 8 data blocks, a 32-byte initial state, and every labeled field in the binary pointing somewhere wrong. Plus a hash chain that turns out not to exist. Reversing the only field that tells the truth: the official scorer itself.

item.title: AfricaHackon: Rooted or Not? Bypassing a Root Check Without Rooting Anything
item.description: Android APK reversing, XOR key recovered, static analysis only. A vault app gates its debug panel behind a root check, but the flag is computed statically. No rooting, no emulator, no Frida needed.
